name: AI System Architect
tag: Turns a business problem into a reviewed AI solution design, from requirements to deployment plan.

scenarios.title: Design a demand forecast
scenarios.ask: Design an AI system to forecast weekly demand for {skus} products across {sites} warehouses.
steps: Problem framer
Defined the goal: cut stockouts without raising inventory. Success metric: forecast error by SKU and site.
Data planner
Needs {history} years of sales, promotions and holidays: about {=round(skus * sites * history * 52 / 1000000, 1)} million rows.
Model selector
Recommended a gradient-boosted model with a simple baseline for comparison.
Architecture
Drew the pipeline: nightly data load, weekly training, forecasts to the planning system.
Governance
Added a drift check and a monthly review with the planning team.
followups: Longer history shows seasonal patterns more than once, which helps the model tell a trend from a one-off. Past about five years the gain is small.
No. It is a planning estimate. The design includes a baseline so you measure the real gain before rollout.

scenarios.title: Review a vendor proposal
scenarios.ask: A vendor proposes a chatbot for {calls} calls a month at {price} cents per conversation. Review the design.
steps: Reader
Pulled the architecture, data flow and pricing from the proposal.
Checklist
Checked 24 design points. 4 are missing: data retention, handoff rules, testing plan and exit terms.
Cost model
Compared the vendor price with an estimated in-house cost of about {=round(8 + 1500000 / calls, 1)} cents per conversation including staff.
Writer
Wrote a review memo with questions for the vendor.

result.title: Proposal review
rows: Ask for missing points before deciding

followups: Not on cost alone. In-house means owning updates, monitoring and support. The memo lists those costs so the comparison is fair.
How you get your data and conversation logs back if you leave. Without them, switching vendors later can be slow and costly.

scenarios.title: Plan deployment and monitoring
scenarios.ask: Our document classifier is ready. Plan deployment for {docs} documents a day with a {acc}% accuracy floor.
steps: Deployment planner
Chose a canary rollout: 10% of traffic for one week, then 50%, then all.
Monitor designer
Set alerts if weekly accuracy on a reviewed sample drops below {acc}%.
Sampling
Plans to review {=max(20, round(docs * 0.01))} documents a day by hand to measure accuracy.
Runbook
Wrote steps for rollback and retraining.
followups: Why send more to people at a higher floor?
A higher floor means the model must be more certain before acting alone, so more borderline documents go to a person.
When accuracy drifts toward the floor, or at least quarterly. The plan watches both.
